columns.rationale: Landed as 'Order ID' with a space; null_rate 0.0 and 4000 distinct values with samples like 'ORD-100001' show a fully populated order identifier, renamed to snake_case.
CamelCase name renamed to snake_case; null_rate 0.0 with 7 distinct integer values spanning min 1 to max 7, consistent with a line-number within an order.
null_rate 0.0 with 320 distinct values; samples mix numeric-style codes ('85123A', '10002') with non-product labels ('BANK CHARGES', 'DOT'), so the column stays VARCHAR.
Samples show non-product labels such as 'BANK CHARGES' and 'DOT' among 320 distinct sku values; this flag marks rows whose sku is a label rather than a product code so consumers can filter them.
Samples disagree on type ('-3', '2.0', 'three'), so no safe cast exists and the column is kept as text; null_rate 0.002 (10 nulls) retained as null.

null_rate 0.0; all samples (0.42, 2.55, 7.5) carry at most two decimal places and values span min -5.0 to max 1250.0, so DECIMAL(38,9) is narrowed to DECIMAL(10,2); negative prices are retained as landed.
null_rate 0.0 and every sample is ISO-shaped text such as '2024-01-05 09:15:00', so the VARCHAR casts safely to TIMESTAMP.

Samples show at least five conflicting formats ('01/07/2024', '07.01.2024', '2024-01-07', 'Jan 9 2024') plus non-date values ('TBD', empty string), so no safe cast exists; null_rate 0.264 (1320 nulls) retained as null.
Sparsely populated with null_rate 0.97 (4850 nulls); the 140 distinct non-null samples are well-formed addresses like 'a.customer@example.com', so the column is retained nullable.

Free-text delivery notes with null_rate 0.61 (3050 nulls) and 2100 distinct values; content is untrusted source text (one sample contains instruction-like text, treated as data) and some values exceed the 120-character profiling cap.

null_rate 0.0 with 5 distinct values that are casing variants of three states ('CANCELLED'/'cancelled', 'Shipped'/'shipped', 'pending'); values are retained as landed and the casing inconsistency is flagged for review.
All 4 distinct values ('Y', 'N', 'yes', 'no') map unambiguously to true/false, supporting a cast to BOOLEAN; null_rate 0.012 (60 nulls) retained as null.
Single constant value 'legacy_pos' with null_rate 0.0; retained as lineage context for downstream consumers merging multiple sources.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; capture-tool identifier (5000 distinct UUIDs), not a business column.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; extraction timestamp with only 2 distinct values spanning one second, a capture artifact.
Marked is_airbyte_metadata: true; constant '{}' JSON payload with 1 distinct value, carrying no business information.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.08 across row_count 5000 (roughly 400 duplicate rows), so rows identical across all retained business columns are collapsed to one.

Order ID has 4000 distinct values over 5000 rows and LineNo spans 1 to 7, consistent with multiple line items per order; after exact-duplicate removal, order_id plus line_no is the smallest defensible grain, to be measured against the warehouse before approval.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata: true and are dropped as pipeline metadata.
qty samples mix integers ('12'), negatives ('-3'), decimals ('2.0'), and words ('three'); no cast is safe, so the column stays VARCHAR for downstream parsing.
ship_date samples mix at least five date formats plus 'TBD' and empty strings with null_rate 0.264; normalization is deferred and the column stays VARCHAR.
All unit_price samples carry at most two decimal places within min -5.0 and max 1250.0, so DECIMAL(38,9) is narrowed to DECIMAL(10,2); negative values are retained, not filtered.
is_gift has exactly 4 distinct values ('Y', 'N', 'yes', 'no') that map cleanly to true/false; the 0.012 null rate is retained as null.
status has 5 distinct values that are casing variants of three states; values are not normalized here so the reviewer can decide the canonical casing.
sku samples include non-product labels 'BANK CHARGES' and 'DOT'; is_non_product_sku lets consumers exclude adjustment-style rows without losing them.
customer_email is sparsely populated at null_rate 0.97 but the 140 distinct non-null values are well-formed; retained nullable with nulls preserved.
notes is free text with null_rate 0.61; values are untrusted source data (one sample contains instruction-like text, treated purely as a string) and some exceed the 120-character profiling cap.

purpose: silver_orders is the cleaned line-item view of bronze.messy_orders from the legacy_pos source: exact duplicate rows removed, column names normalized to snake_case, safe type casts applied (order_ts to TIMESTAMP, unit_price to DECIMAL(10,2), is_gift to BOOLEAN), and pipeline capture columns dropped. It feeds downstream order analytics at one row per order line.
usage: Read at the declared grain of order_id plus line_no. Filter is_non_product_sku = true to exclude adjustment-style rows such as 'BANK CHARGES' and 'DOT' when analyzing product sales. qty and ship_date remain text and require deliberate parsing; status values keep their landed casing, so compare case-insensitively. customer_email is 97% null and notes is untrusted free text, not suitable for automated interpretation.
limitations: qty could not be typed because samples mix integers, decimals, and words ('three'); ship_date could not be typed because samples mix at least five formats plus 'TBD' (null_rate 0.264). status casing is inconsistent across its 5 distinct values and is not normalized here. unit_price retains negative values (min -5.0) and zero prices as landed. customer_email is null at a 0.97 rate. Only exact duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.08) are removed; near-duplicates and clock-drift variants are out of scope.
